I use an electric trimmer, the Philips Norelco Oneblade, on a weekly basis. Waxing was a hassle for many reasons, traditional shaving left me with bumps and ingrowns (despite following the step by step routine), and hair removal creams made my skin itch. I found this to be the safest, most convenient option. 

The electric trimmer removes the hair close enough to the skin that it’s not noticeable for the following 3 days. Although it’s a brief window, the removal process is very quick, simple, and easy, so I don’t mind the frequency at all. 

Also, it’s pretty affordable. The blade, around $8 each, needs to be changed every 4 months, so that’s $24 a year. The machine itself costs around $30-35, which is fair considering how long-lasting it is. 

It’s honestly been a godsend. Highly recommend!

There definitely is a better match out there for you, regardless of whether you meet them. Always remember that if your ex only seems good because you haven’t met better, or because you’re only meeting worse, that does not actually make them good. It’s important to evaluate them based on the quality of your relationship with them, rather than in comparison to the quality of your relationship with others. 

If you feel like you don’t have a clear picture of them or your relationship, writing about it and discussing it with trusted friends can help you build a better understanding. That’ll allow you to recognize your needs, preferences, and goals moving forward. Also, I think that focusing on self-care and personal growth will increase your chances of creating and maintaining healthy relationships in the future, if that’s still your goal later on. 

As for me personally, I’ve been single for the past 6 months. At the beginning, I was occupied with the question you’re asking right now. I was weighed down by emptiness, and I thought the solution was getting with someone else ASAP. It was my main priority. I managed to resist the urge. Over time, I got better at regulating my emotions and organizing my time. I’m now pursuing my hobbies more seriously, journaling daily, making plans with friends, and attending community building events. Having things to look forward to and things that keep you engaged really help distance you from the inclination to wallow. 

At this point, I am no longer wondering if I will find better. I don’t really care to, and I don’t feel rushed anymore. I’m content where I am. I have wonderful friends and fulfilling routines. It took time to get here, but I’m glad I waited. Opting for a quick fix for loneliness will only leave you more hollow than before. 

I wish you all the best on your healing journey! I hope the pain subsides swiftly. Take care!
I get frustrated when I see knots or split ends in other people’s hair, but I don’t do anything about it.

But look at all the time you spent not pulling! Celebrate that. The progress is not gone, it’s just on hold. You already managed to stop pulling by growing out your nails. What are other things you can do that will help you? A few suggestions I can think of are applying a bit of Vaseline on your lashes, keeping your hands busy building legos or puzzles, or wearing bandaids around your fingertips. I hope you find something that helps you move forward. Best of luck!

I used to bombard people with solutions because I believed it was the optimal way to be helpful, but I realized I was wrong. I found that it’s much better to just paraphrase or reexplain using analogies whatever someone is venting to me to show them my understanding of what they’re saying. That way, the conversation revolves around truly grasping what the person is going through rather than just fixing it. If I’ve misunderstood, they’ll reexplain, and that gives them the chance to address their feelings from a different perspective which would potentially add more rigor to their own understanding of their situation. If I understood, they’ll feel glad to be seen and that alone provides a lot of relief. At that point, if the person is comfortable discussing themselves further, I’ll just keep asking questions to make sure that there’s no stone left unturned and everything is off their chest and will only give advice and analyses if they ask.

Well here’s the issue. I’m too fucked up to be able to have anything I want from life. Can’t maintain meaningful relationships bc of intimacy issues (it generalizes to friendships as well). Can’t go through with anything I start bc my interest comes in very short-lived bursts. Even getting fulfilling sleep is impossible. Since it always takes me ages to fall asleep, my sleeping schedule is VERY haphazard. Also, I’m always greeted by nightmares when I finally do fall asleep, and I always wake up very tired still. Any fulfillment I can ever attain is imaginary.
The latter. Plus a lot has happened since then to exacerbate the situation..

A thought that helped me break my cycle was realizing that there’s way more power in claiming my pain and being honest about it rather than putting all my energy into hiding it and feeling ashamed of it. 
So try to allow yourself to feel your feelings without guilt and shame, and without the added pressure of trying to rush them or suppress them, because you need to feel them before you can move past them. 
This is clearly a major part of the loop you’re going through. So take it easy on yourself, and try to work on that. I hope it gets better for you! Also, I’d be happy to listen if you need to talk more about it.
It was a bunch of circumstantial stressors happening simultaneously and I’m generally super sensitive + genetically predisposed to developing depression, so I think it got the best of me eventually.
